raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a radial (donut) chart that compares the distribution of characters across different categories, with a central label indicating "Virtual Characters" and "Real Characters" as the primary divisions. The chart is divided into two main sections: "Virtual Characters" on the left, which includes Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, and "Real Characters" on the right, which includes Custom Characters, Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers. The "Virtual Characters" section is represented by a large light blue ring, while the "Real Characters" section is divided into smaller segments in varying shades of green and pink. The "Custom Characters" segment is colored pink, while all other "Real Characters" segments are in different shades of green. The "Virtual Characters" category is the largest segment, occupying the majority of the chart, followed by "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Game Characters," which are all smaller but still significant. The "Real Characters" segments are smaller in comparison, with "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers" each occupying a small portion of the chart. The "Custom Characters" segment is slightly larger than the others in the "Real Characters" group. There is no legend, and the percentages are not explicitly labeled within the segments, but the relative sizes of the segments can be visually compared. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top, with the "Virtual Characters" section on the left and the "Real Characters" section on the right.
raw_responses.English: DESCRIPTION: The chart is a radial (or pie) chart that visually represents the distribution of different character categories, with a central focus on "Virtual Characters" and surrounding segments for other types. There are 12 distinct categories shown: "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," "Game Characters," "Real Characters," "Custom Characters," "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers." The central "Virtual Characters" segment is large and light blue, while the surrounding categories are arranged in a circular pattern around it, with varying sizes and colors. The outer segments are color-coded: "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Game Characters" are light blue; "Real Characters" is green; "Custom Characters" is red; and the remaining categories ("Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," "Influencers") are in progressively lighter shades of green. No percentage labels are visible inside the slices, and there is no legend; labels are placed directly adjacent to each segment. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order, with no apparent visual emphasis such as exploded slices.
raw_responses.German: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a radial bar chart that visually represents the distribution of different character categories, with the central label "Virtual Characters" indicating the primary focus. The chart is divided into two main sections: "Virtual Characters" and "Real Characters," each further subdivided into specific categories. The "Virtual Characters" section includes Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, all represented by light blue segments of varying sizes. The "Real Characters" section includes Custom Characters, Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, with segments in shades of green and pink. The segments are arranged in a circular pattern around the center, with the size of each segment corresponding to its relative proportion. The chart does not display explicit percentage values within the segments, nor does it include a separate legend; instead, the labels are directly placed near their respective segments. The arrangement appears to follow a clockwise order, starting from the top with "Comic Characters" and progressing through the categories.
